# Hedonic treadmill

People adapt. A raise, a new flat, a faster bike: each lifts satisfaction for a while and then becomes the baseline from which the next want is measured.

## Why it matters for the essay

Adaptation means satisfaction does not accumulate. The level of contentment returns to roughly where it started while the level of consumption ratchets up. The treadmill is the reason that getting what we want so rarely ends the wanting.

## Limits

Adaptation is not complete for everything. Noise, a long commute and chronic pain resist it. Some gains (time with friends, autonomy) seem to fade more slowly than gains in income.

Compare [[The wanting-liking split]].
